title: Cluster Node Minimum Memory Provisioning
real_world_story: A cloud platform autoscaler is provisioning a Kubernetes cluster with K identical worker nodes. An application deployment manifest contains N microservice pods that must be deployed in their exact declared sequence: pod 1, pod 2, ..., pod N. Each node can host a contiguous subsegment of pods from this sequence. Pod i requires r_i GB of RAM. The cloud infrastructure team needs to provision nodes with the minimum possible RAM capacity C (in GB) such that all N pods can be distributed across at most K nodes without any node exceeding capacity C.
problem_statement: Given an array of N integers representing RAM requirements r_1, r_2, ..., r_N and an integer K, find the minimum integer node capacity C such that the pods can be partitioned into at most K contiguous subarrays where the sum of each subarray does not exceed C.
task: Find and print the minimum per-node RAM capacity C.
input_format:
The first line contains two space-separated integers N and K, the number of pods and the maximum number of worker nodes.
The second line contains N space-separated integers r_1, r_2, ..., r_N, representing the RAM required by each pod.
output_format: Print a single integer representing the minimum node RAM capacity C.

examples.explanation: With node capacity C = 9, the pods can be partitioned into 2 nodes: Node 1: [1, 2, 3] (sum 6 <= 9); Node 2: [4, 5] (sum 9 <= 9). Any capacity smaller than 9 would require at least 3 nodes.
With K = 4 nodes for 4 pods, each node can host exactly 1 pod. The minimum capacity is the maximum single pod requirement: 40 GB.

real_world_takeaway: Binary search on answer combined with greedy feasibility verification rapidly determines optimal cloud hardware provisioning boundaries without brute-force enumeration.
